title: Spend Before Death and the Day of Loss

paragraphs.text: The hypocrites tell others not to spend on the companions of the Messenger so that they will scatter, not realizing that the treasures of the heavens and the earth belong to Allah. They also boast that when they return to Madinah, the more powerful will drive out the weaker. But all honor belongs to Allah, His Messenger and the believers. The believers are warned not to let their wealth and children distract them from remembering Allah, since those who do so are the losers. They should spend from what Allah has given them before death arrives, when a person might beg for a short delay so that he could give charity and become righteous. Allah never delays a soul once its appointed time has come.

A new surah begins with everything in creation glorifying Allah, to whom belong all rule and all praise. He created human beings, yet some of them disbelieve while others believe. He created the heavens and the earth with truth, shaped people and made their forms beautiful, and all will return to Him. He knows what they hide and what they show, and even what lies within their hearts. Earlier nations disbelieved and tasted the bad result of their choices. When their messengers brought clear proofs, they asked whether mere human beings could guide them, and so they turned away. Allah did not need them at all, for He is Free of need and Praiseworthy.

The disbelievers insist that they will never be raised again, but the Prophet is told to swear by his Lord that they certainly will, and that they will be informed of their deeds, which is easy for Allah. Therefore people should believe in Allah, His Messenger and the Qur'an. The Day of Gathering will be a day of mutual loss and gain, when believers who did good will have their sins removed and enter eternal gardens, while those who denied Allah's verses will live in the Fire forever. No disaster happens without Allah's permission, and He guides the heart of whoever believes. The duty of the Messenger is only to deliver the message clearly.

hardWords.m: to take attention away from something
to say something strongly and firmly
